\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پھرتی} (phurtī)}{پھرتی (phurtī)}]{\ur{پھرتی} (phurtī) — agility; quickness}

\label{lesson:UR-C522-phurti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a winner, then the Urdu for a defeat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پھرتی}}
\textbf{\ur{پھرتی}} — \emph{phurtī} — \textquotedblleft{}agility; quickness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{کھلاڑی} \ur{میں} \ur{بڑی} \ur{پھرتی} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{is khilāṛī meṅ baṛī phurtī hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This player is very quick on his feet.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پھرتی}} (\emph{phurtī}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{phurtī}, \textquotedblleft{}activity\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{sphurati}, \textquotedblleft{}darts, springs\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13849).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phurtī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phurtī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{is khilāṛī meṅ baṛī phurtī hai.} — This player is very quick on his feet.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a winner, then the Urdu for a defeat, then say \emph{phurtī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{پھرتی} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Agility; quickness\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لچکنا} (lachaknā)}{لچکنا (lachaknā)}]{\ur{لچکنا} (lachaknā) — to bend without breaking; to flex}

\label{lesson:UR-C522-lachakna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a defeat, then the Urdu for agility.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لچکنا}}
\textbf{\ur{لچکنا}} — \emph{lachaknā} — \textquotedblleft{}to bend without breaking; to flex\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{کھلاڑی} \ur{کا} \ur{جسم} \ur{بہت} \ur{لچکتا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{is khilāṛī kā jism bahut lachaktā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This player's body is very supple.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{شاخ} \ur{ہوا} \ur{میں} \ur{لچکی}, \emph{voh shākh hawā meṅ lachkī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لچکنا}} (\emph{lachaknā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{lacaknā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be bent\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*lacc}, \textquotedblleft{}bend, sway\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 10907).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lachaknā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lachaknā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{is khilāṛī kā jism bahut lachaktā hai.} — This player's body is very supple.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a defeat, then the Urdu for agility, then say \emph{lachaknā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{لچکنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To bend without breaking; to flex\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لڑھکانا} (luṛhkānā)}{لڑھکانا (luṛhkānā)}]{\ur{لڑھکانا} (luṛhkānā) — to roll (something) along}

\label{lesson:UR-C522-lurhkana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for agility, then the Urdu for to bend without breaking.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لڑھکانا}}
\textbf{\ur{لڑھکانا}} — \emph{luṛhkānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to roll (something) along\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بچے} \ur{نے} \ur{گیند} \ur{میری} \ur{طرف} \ur{لڑھکائی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bachche ne gend merī taraf luṛhkāī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The child rolled the ball towards me.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{پتھر} \ur{لڑھکایا}, \emph{us ne patthar luṛhkāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لڑھکانا}} (\emph{luṛhkānā}) is the causative of \emph{luṛhaknā}, \textquotedblleft{}to roll\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists under Sanskrit \emph{luṭhati}, \textquotedblleft{}rolls, wallows\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11079).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{luṛhkānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bachche ne gend merī taraf luṛhkāī.} — The child rolled the ball towards me.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for agility, then the Urdu for to bend without breaking, then say \emph{luṛhkānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دوڑانا} (dauṛānā)}{دوڑانا (dauṛānā)}]{\ur{دوڑانا} (dauṛānā) — to make (someone) run}

\label{lesson:UR-C522-daurana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to bend without breaking, then the Urdu for to roll (something) along.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دوڑانا}}
\textbf{\ur{دوڑانا}} — \emph{dauṛānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to make (someone) run\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{استاد} \ur{نے} \ur{لڑکوں} \ur{کو} \ur{میدان} \ur{میں} \ur{دوڑایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ustād ne laṛkoṅ ko maidān meṅ dauṛāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The teacher made the boys run round the field.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{گھوڑا} \ur{دوڑایا}, \emph{us ne ghoṛā dauṛāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{دوڑانا}} (\emph{dauṛānā}) is the causative of \emph{dauṛnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to run\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists under Sanskrit \emph{dravati}, \textquotedblleft{}runs\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 6624).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}
